name: Vilvoorde (Vilvorde), near Brussels
desc: William Tyndale, translator of the English New Testament, was imprisoned here and executed in early October 1536.

name: Providence, Rhode Island
desc: Roger Williams founded Providence in 1636 and helped found what became the first Baptist church in America.

name: Topsfield, Massachusetts
desc: Birthplace of Asael Smith, Joseph Smith's grandfather. He brought his family back here after 1785 before moving to Vermont in 1791.

name: Gilsum, New Hampshire
desc: Lucy Mack was born here in July 1775. Her father, Solomon Mack, took to his bed here in the fall of 1810.

name: Tunbridge, Vermont
desc: The Smiths cleared a hill farm here. Lucy Mack and Joseph Smith were married in Tunbridge on January 24, 1796.

name: Randolph, Vermont
desc: Lucy fell gravely ill here and made a covenant with God that she would serve him if her life was spared.

name: Sharon, Vermont (Joseph Smith Birthplace)
desc: Joseph Smith Jr. was born in a rented farmhouse here. A granite obelisk was dedicated on the site in 1905.

name: Lebanon, New Hampshire
desc: The family moved here in 1811. During the typhoid epidemic, young Joseph underwent leg surgery without alcohol, refusing to be bound.

name: Norwich, Vermont
desc: The Smiths rented a farm here. Crop failures, ending with the cold of 1816, sent them west to New York.
cht: The Boy Who Would Not Be Bound

name: Palmyra, New York
desc: Lucy and her eight children joined Joseph Sr. here after some three hundred miles of winter travel. The family first rented in the village.
cht: The Boy Who Would Not Be Bound

name: Smith Family Farm, Manchester, New York
desc: The Smiths' log house and later their frame home stood on their farm here, south of Palmyra.
cht: The Boy Who Would Not Be Bound

name: The Sacred Grove
desc: The woods west of the Smith home where Joseph went to pray and, as he later recounted, saw a pillar of light: the First Vision.

name: Hill Cumorah
desc: The hill about three miles from the Smith farm where Joseph said the plates were buried. He received them here in September 1827.

name: Harmony, Pennsylvania (Priesthood Restoration Site)
desc: Emma Hale's home town. Here Joseph translated most of the Book of Mormon, and near the Susquehanna River he and Oliver Cowdery testified that John the Baptist conferred the priesthood on May 15, 1829.

name: South Bainbridge (now Afton), New York
desc: Joseph was brought before a justice here in March 1826. He and Emma Hale were married here on January 18, 1827.

name: Colesville, New York
desc: Home of the Knight family, among the first branches of the church. Joseph, Emma and Oliver came here in June 1830.
cht: By the Gift and Power of God

name: Peter Whitmer Farm, Fayette, New York
desc: The translation was finished at the Whitmer home, and the church was organized in the Whitmers' log house on April 6, 1830.
cht: By the Gift and Power of God

name: E. B. Grandin's printing office, Palmyra
desc: Five thousand copies of the Book of Mormon were printed and bound here; the first copies went on sale on March 26, 1830.
cht: By the Gift and Power of God

name: Buffalo, New York
desc: Lucy Mack Smith's company of about eighty from Fayette found the harbor choked with ice on their way to Ohio.

name: John Johnson Farm, Hiram, Ohio
desc: Joseph and Emma lived here with John and Elsa Johnson. The vision of February 16, 1832 was received here, and a mob tarred and feathered Joseph in late March 1832.

name: Independence, Jackson County, Missouri
desc: The Saints began settling here in 1831. A mob destroyed the church's printing office in July 1833, and the Saints were driven from the county by November.

name: Fairport Harbor, Ohio
desc: Lake Erie landing for Saints bound for Kirtland. Joseph and Hyrum met their grandmother Mary Duty Smith here on May 17, 1836.

name: Kirtland, Ohio · Newel K. Whitney store
desc: Joseph arrived here by sleigh. The upper room later held the School of the Prophets, beginning January 22, 1833.

name: Kirtland Temple
desc: Built of sandstone rubble covered with bluish-gray stucco, dedicated March 27, 1836. Joseph and Oliver testified of the visions of April 3, 1836 here.

name: Far West, Missouri
desc: The Saints' town on the prairie of Caldwell County. Joseph and other leaders were taken prisoner here under a flag of truce.

name: Gallatin, Missouri
desc: A fight broke out at the polls here on Election Day 1838; in mid-October Latter-day Saint forces raided Gallatin and Millport.

name: Crooked River battle site
desc: Latter-day Saints clashed before dawn with a state militia unit; Apostle David W. Patten was among those killed.

name: Hawn's Mill
desc: A small settlement on Shoal Creek where a mob attacked Latter-day Saint families. Amanda Barnes Smith's son Alma survived.

name: Richmond, Missouri
desc: After hearings here, Joseph, Hyrum and four others were sent to the jail at Liberty.

name: Liberty Jail, Missouri
desc: Joseph and his companions were held through the winter in the lower room of this jail, where Joseph wrote the letters from which Doctrine and Covenants 121 and 122 are drawn.

name: Quincy, Illinois
desc: Refugee Saints crossing from Missouri found the people of Quincy kinder than they had expected.

name: Montrose, Iowa
desc: Across the river from Nauvoo. Joseph came here during the malaria season, and Wilford Woodruff recorded the healing of Elijah Fordham.

name: Nauvoo (formerly Commerce), Illinois
desc: A muddy river landing called Commerce, drained and built into one of the largest cities in Illinois.

name: Mount of Olives, Jerusalem
desc: Orson Hyde climbed the mount before dawn and offered a prayer dedicating the land "for the gathering together of Judah's scattered remnants."

name: Nauvoo Temple
desc: Built on the bluff above the city; the Saints received temple ordinances here before leaving for the West in 1846.

name: Joseph Smith's Red Brick Store, Nauvoo
desc: Twenty women met with Joseph in the large upper room here and organized the Female Relief Society of Nauvoo.

name: Carthage Jail, Illinois
desc: Joseph and Hyrum Smith were killed here by a mob; John Taylor was wounded and Willard Richards survived.
cht: Carthage, and the Work Rolls On
